newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD could accept 45 pct tax rate - paper.
newsitem.headline: German SPD could accept 45 pct tax rate - paper.

text.p: A key member of the German opposition Social Democrats (SPD) was cited on Wednesday as saying he could accept a lowering of the top German income tax rate, a part of a major tax reform the government wants to introduce.
SPD parliamentary business manager Peter Struck was quoted in the Cologne-based Express newspaper as saying he could accept a cut in the top tax rate from the current 53 percent to 45 percent.

While such a cut is a move in the direction of the 39 percent top tax rate that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government is seeking to introduce, Struck nonetheless said he believed that a rate lower than 45 percent could not be financed.
The SPD, which controls the upper house of parliament, in April pulled out of talks aimed at getting cross-party support for the reform.
The matter is to be sent to arbitration after which, if no agreement is then found, it will be debated in parliament.
